days.title: Core Generative AI Concepts, ML Approaches, and Prompting

concepts.heading: AI, Machine Learning, Generative AI, and NLP
concepts.body: These terms are nested like circles. Artificial intelligence (AI) is the broad goal: software that does tasks we associate with human intelligence, such as understanding language, recognizing images or making decisions. Machine learning (ML) is one way to reach that goal. Instead of writing explicit rules, you let a system learn patterns from data and then make predictions on new data. Generative AI (gen AI) is a branch of ML in which models learn the patterns in very large amounts of data well enough to create new content such as text, images, code, audio or video. A spam filter is ML but not generative, because it only classifies each email into a fixed label. A model that drafts the reply to that email is generative, because it composes new content. Natural language processing (NLP) is the part of AI concerned with human language: reading text, understanding intent, translating, summarizing and writing. Modern NLP is dominated by large language models, so NLP is the field and an LLM is one powerful tool inside it.

concepts.heading: Foundation Models, Multimodal Models, LLMs, and Tokens
concepts.body: Before foundation models, a team usually collected labeled data and trained a new model for each task: one for sentiment, one for translation, one for fraud. A foundation model, also called a base model, is trained once on a massive and broad dataset and can then be adapted to many tasks, often just by prompting it or by tuning it lightly. For a business this means one investment supports many use cases and teams start from a capable model rather than from zero. A multimodal foundation model works with more than one modality, where a modality is a type of data such as text, images, audio, video or code. Gemini is Google's multimodal model family. A large language model (LLM) is a foundation model trained on very large text collections; it learns statistical patterns of language, so it can continue, answer, summarize, translate or rewrite text. LLMs read text as tokens: small chunks that can be a short word, a piece of a longer word, a number or a punctuation mark. Usage and limits are commonly measured in tokens, so longer prompts and longer answers use more of them, and the token count is not simply the word count.

concepts.heading: Diffusion Models
concepts.body: A diffusion model is the technique behind many text-to-image generators. In plain terms it learns by studying how images gradually turn into random noise, and then it learns to reverse that process. To create a picture, it starts from random noise and removes the noise in many small steps, guided by the text prompt, until a coherent image appears. The important business idea is that a diffusion model creates a new image. It does not look up or copy a stored image, which separates it from image search, and it does not group existing images, which separates it from clustering. If a question describes turning a written description into a picture, the model type being described is an image generation model, and diffusion is the common technique behind it.

concepts.heading: Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning
concepts.body: The exam names three ML approaches, and a two-question test sorts any scenario. First ask whether the data comes with the correct answer. Supervised learning trains on labeled data: each example has inputs and the correct answer, called the label. The model learns the mapping and predicts labels for new inputs. Classification, such as spam or not spam or loan repaid or defaulted, and regression, such as predicting a price, are supervised tasks. Unsupervised learning works on unlabeled data and looks for structure on its own. Typical tasks are clustering, such as discovering customer segments nobody defined in advance, association, such as items bought together, and dimensionality reduction, which simplifies data with many attributes. Second ask whether the system learns by acting and receiving feedback. Reinforcement learning has an agent take actions in an environment and receive rewards or penalties. Over many trials it learns a policy, a strategy for which action to take in each situation. A simulated warehouse robot rewarded for fast, collision-free deliveries is the classic example, and no dataset of correct answers exists in advance.

concepts.heading: Prompt Engineering Versus Prompt Tuning
concepts.body: A prompt is the input given to a model: instructions, context, examples and the question. Prompt engineering is the practice of designing and iterating on prompts so the model produces better and more reliable results. It needs no training: the model is unchanged and only the input changes. Typical levers are a clear task and output format, context such as audience, tone and length, examples of the desired answer, and iteration where you review outputs and refine. Prompt tuning is different. It is a parameter-efficient tuning technique in which a small set of learned values, sometimes called a soft prompt, is trained on example data and attached to the input, while the large model's own weights stay frozen. It needs a set of examples and a training run, but far less than retraining the whole model. The practical rule is a staircase of effort. Start with prompt engineering because it takes minutes to hours and needs no data. Consider tuning when careful prompts still fall short and you have quality examples of the behavior you want. Training a model from scratch needs enormous data, compute and expertise and is rarely justified for a business team. A team with no labeled data, no ML staff and a one-week deadline should therefore improve its prompts.

examPoints: Nesting: AI is the goal, ML is learning from data, gen AI is the ML branch that creates new content, and NLP is the language-focused field of AI.
Labeled data with a known answer means supervised, unlabeled data where structure is discovered means unsupervised, and an agent that earns rewards in an environment means reinforcement learning.
Prompt engineering changes only the input and needs no training, while prompt tuning trains a small set of learned values on examples with the model's weights frozen; the cheapest lever comes first.

quiz.q: A bank has years of loan records, each marked repaid or defaulted, and wants to predict the outcome for new applications. Which machine learning approach fits?
choices: Supervised learning, because each record already carries the correct answer to learn from
Unsupervised learning, because the bank mainly wants to discover hidden groups in its loan history
Reinforcement learning, because each lending decision either earns or loses the bank some money
Diffusion modeling, because the bank wants to create realistic new loan records for testing
quiz.explain: The records are labeled and the task predicts a category, which is classification and therefore supervised learning. Choice B is tempting because the bank has a lot of historical data, but unsupervised learning is for data without answers where the goal is to discover structure.

quiz.q: A team with no labeled data and no ML engineers has one week to make a model's replies sound consistent with the brand. What is the best first step?
choices: Collect thousands of labeled examples and then train a brand new model from scratch
Run a prompt tuning job on a large set of brand examples that staff have labeled by hand
Write clearer prompts with a defined role, format and a few examples, then iterate
Switch to a diffusion model because it is the newest kind of foundation model available
quiz.explain: Prompt engineering needs no data pipeline or training and can be done in hours, which fits the constraints. Choice B is tempting because prompt tuning is cheaper than full retraining, but it still needs example data and a training run, which this team lacks.

days.recap: AI is the broad goal, ML learns from data and gen AI creates new content; foundation models, multimodal models and LLMs (which read tokens) are the building blocks, diffusion models create images from noise, ML approaches are supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement, and prompt engineering is the cheapest lever before prompt tuning.

days.title: The ML Lifecycle and Google Cloud Tools for Each Stage

concepts.heading: The Five Stages in Order
concepts.body: The exam describes the machine learning lifecycle as five stages. Data ingestion collects data from sources such as streams, files and databases into a place where it can be used. Data preparation cleans, transforms, labels and organizes that data so it is suitable for learning. Model training lets the algorithm learn from the prepared data and evaluates the result. Model deployment makes the model available to produce predictions or content for applications and users. Model management keeps the model healthy over time by versioning it, monitoring performance and drift, retraining and automating the workflow. For a leader, the useful habit is to ask which stage a problem belongs to, because each stage has its own Google Cloud tools. Many Google Cloud ML tools sit on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, which was previously named Vertex AI.

concepts.heading: Stages 1 and 2: Ingestion and Preparation Tools
concepts.body: Ingestion is about getting data into Google Cloud, and the tool depends on how the data arrives. Pub/Sub is messaging for streaming events from apps, devices and services, and it decouples producers from consumers. Cloud Storage is the landing zone for files and objects. BigQuery is the analytics warehouse for structured data. Dataflow processes and moves streaming or batch data, often reading from Pub/Sub and writing to BigQuery. Preparation turns collected data into training-ready data, and its quality shapes everything after it. Preparation includes cleaning, removing duplicates, handling missing values, standardizing formats and units, joining sources and labeling. Useful tools are Dataflow for scalable transformation pipelines, BigQuery for SQL-based transformation and analysis of large structured datasets, Dataproc for managed Apache Spark and Hadoop for teams with existing jobs, and managed datasets on Agent Platform that organize image and tabular data for training. If a scenario says data has already arrived but is messy, the stage is preparation, not ingestion.

concepts.heading: Stage 3: Training Options
concepts.body: Training is where the algorithm learns from the prepared data. Agent Platform offers choices on a spectrum from convenience to control. AutoML lets Google Cloud choose the approach and train a model from your managed dataset, such as tabular or image data, without writing training code, which suits teams without deep ML skills. Custom training means your own code, written with frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch, running on managed training infrastructure, and it suits teams that need full control. Workbench, formerly Vertex AI Workbench, is a managed Jupyter-based notebook environment integrated with BigQuery and Cloud Storage, where data scientists explore data, prototype and develop models, and then launch larger training jobs. A scenario with limited ML expertise, tabular data and a wish for managed infrastructure points to AutoML. A scenario in which scientists need a place to write and iterate on code points to Workbench.

concepts.heading: Stages 4 and 5: Deployment and Management
concepts.body: Deployment makes a trained model available to applications. On Agent Platform there are two patterns. Online inference deploys the model to an endpoint that returns low-latency predictions to apps in real time, for example while a user interacts with an app. Batch inference runs predictions over a large dataset at once when instant answers are not needed, such as scoring every customer overnight. Management begins after launch because models decay. When the real world changes, the data the model sees in production differs from the data it was trained on. This is drift when input or prediction distributions change over time, and skew when production data differs from training data. Model Monitoring (v1, the generally available version, set up on endpoints) tracks input features and predictions for drift and skew and raises alerts. Model Registry is the central place to organize and track models and their versions, evaluate them and deploy a selected version. Pipelines automate the workflow as connected steps for data preparation, training, evaluation and deployment, which makes runs repeatable and auditable and is a core part of MLOps. Feature Store serves and shares ML features consistently.

concepts.heading: Training Versus Inference, and the Stage-to-Tool Map
concepts.body: Two phases are easy to confuse. Training is the learning phase: the algorithm processes data and adjusts the model's parameters. It is compute-intensive and happens before the model is used, and again whenever you retrain or tune. Inference is the usage phase: the finished model receives new input, such as a prompt, and produces an output. It happens every time a user or application calls the model. When a company uses an existing foundation model through a managed service, the provider already paid the training cost and the company pays for inference when it uses the model. Tuning adds a training step for the company. Keep a one-line map for the exam. Ingestion: Pub/Sub for streams, Cloud Storage for files, Dataflow for moving data. Preparation: Dataflow, BigQuery, Dataproc and managed datasets. Training: AutoML, custom training and Workbench on Agent Platform. Deployment: Agent Platform endpoints for online and batch inference. Management: Model Registry, Pipelines, Model Monitoring and Feature Store. To eliminate wrong choices, ask what a service fundamentally does: messaging does not train, and a model repository does not collect raw data.

examPoints: The five stages in order are data ingestion, data preparation, model training, model deployment and model management; scenarios usually give a symptom and ask for the stage or tool.
Pub/Sub ingests streams, Dataflow and BigQuery prepare data, AutoML or custom training or Workbench train, Agent Platform endpoints deploy, and Model Registry, Model Monitoring and Pipelines manage.
Training is the learning phase done before use; inference is each call to the finished model, which is the cost a company mainly pays when it uses an existing foundation model.

quiz.q: A ride-sharing company must capture a continuous stream of location events from millions of phones and make them available for later model training. Which Google Cloud service fits the ingestion stage?
choices: Model Registry, because it keeps a central record of every model version
Pub/Sub, because it receives streaming events and decouples senders from consumers
AutoML, because it trains models without any code from managed datasets
Workbench, because it gives data scientists a managed notebook environment
quiz.explain: Ingestion of continuous events calls for a streaming messaging service, which is Pub/Sub. Choice C is tempting because AutoML is a Google Cloud ML product, but it belongs to the training stage and does not collect data.

quiz.q: A fraud model performed well at launch, but months later its accuracy has fallen because customer behavior changed. Which capability helps detect this and which stage is it?
choices: Model Monitoring in the model management stage, which tracks drift and skew
Dataflow in the data ingestion stage, which moves streaming data around
Online inference in the deployment stage, which returns real-time predictions
Managed datasets in the data preparation stage, which organize image data
quiz.explain: Changing real-world data is drift, and tracking it with alerts is Model Monitoring in the management stage. Choice C is tempting because the model is already deployed, but deployment only serves predictions and does not watch quality over time.

days.recap: The lifecycle runs data ingestion (Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Dataflow), preparation (Dataflow, BigQuery, Dataproc), training (AutoML, custom training, Workbench), deployment (endpoints for online or batch inference) and management (Model Registry, Pipelines, Model Monitoring); training is the learning phase and inference is each use of the finished model.

days.title: Choosing a Foundation Model and Gen AI Use Cases

concepts.heading: Modality and Context Window
concepts.body: Choosing a foundation model starts with the output the business needs, because a model can only produce what it was built to produce. The modality of a model is the kind of data it takes in and puts out. Large language models read and write text, and in many cases code. Image generation models create pictures from a text description. Multimodal models accept or produce more than one modality, for example text plus images. Video generation models create short clips from text or reference images. In Model Garden on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform you can filter the catalog by the task you want the model to perform. A multimodal model fits mixed inputs such as a scanned form, photos and a note. The second early filter is the context window: the amount of information, measured in tokens, that a model can take into account at one time, including your prompt, any attached documents, the conversation so far and the answer. If the input is larger than the window, the model cannot see all of it, so long contracts and long chat histories need a model with a large enough window. Window sizes change, so do not memorize numbers.

concepts.heading: Security, Availability, and Reliability
concepts.body: For regulated businesses, security, privacy and data governance can matter more than raw model quality. Ask before choosing a model or platform: will the provider train its models on my prompts and data? Google Cloud states that it does not use customer data to train or fine-tune AI and ML models without the customer's prior permission or instruction, and this applies to the managed models on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Can I control where data is processed and who holds the encryption keys? Data residency choices and customer-managed encryption keys address this. Who can access the model and the data? Identity and Access Management (IAM) answers that. Availability and reliability matter once a feature faces customers, because it behaves like any production service: it must be up when customers need it and cope with spikes in traffic. Ask whether the model is offered as a managed service, so that the provider handles serving infrastructure, scaling and operations. Self-hosting an open model gives control, but your team becomes responsible for capacity and uptime.

concepts.heading: Performance and Cost
concepts.body: Foundation models come in sizes and tiers, and Google's own lineup includes both kinds. Larger, more capable models handle complex reasoning and open-ended tasks, but they usually respond more slowly and cost more per request. Smaller or lightweight tiers are designed for high-volume, latency-sensitive work at lower cost. Choose by defining what good enough means for the task: accuracy, response time and cost per request. A simple, high-volume job such as sorting support messages into three labels favors a smaller and faster model, while a task that reasons over many documents may justify a larger one. Start with the smaller tier, test it on real samples, and move up in capability only if the test shows a gap. Cost also includes more than model calls: data preparation, integration, evaluation and the staff time to run the solution all count, so a managed service that needs less operation can be cheaper overall even when its per-request cost looks higher.

concepts.heading: Fine-Tuning and Customization
concepts.body: Customizing a model follows a staircase of effort, and Google's guidance is to start with the cheapest step. Prompting a pre-trained model is the quickest and cheapest start. Clear instructions and a few examples often capture tone and format, and it suits rapid prototyping and cases with little labeled data. Grounding, which connects the model to trusted data at answer time, is the next step when answers must reflect company facts; later days cover it in detail. Tuning, also called fine-tuning, retrains the model on your own labeled examples so it adapts to your domain, style or syntax. Google recommends starting with prompting and moving to tuning if required to improve results or fix recurring errors. Tuning works best with a good set of labeled examples whose format matches what the model will see in production, and well-labeled data matters more than sheer quantity. Training from scratch is rare because it needs huge datasets and compute. If the company has no labeled examples, prompting or grounding is the realistic route.

concepts.heading: Gen AI Use Cases: Create, Summarize, Discover, Automate
concepts.body: The exam groups business uses of gen AI into four verbs. Create means generating new content such as marketing copy, product images, draft code, audio or video. Summarize means condensing long material into key points, such as meeting notes, reports and call transcripts; the value is time, since people review a paragraph instead of a thirty-minute recording. Discover means helping people find and understand information across large collections, often through natural-language search and question answering that cites sources. Google Cloud offers Gemini Enterprise and Agent Search for this. Automate means taking over repeatable steps in a process, such as answering common requests, triaging tickets or filling forms from documents, with escalation to people for unusual cases. Two further examples in the guide are data analysis, where a model turns a plain-language question into a query and explains the result, which lets more people get answers without waiting for an analyst, and personalized user experiences. Across all four, good practice is the same: check summaries and answers against sources, keep people in the loop for decisions with real impact, and measure quality after launch.

examPoints: Model choice starts with modality (the output you need and the inputs you have) and context window (how many tokens the model can consider at once).
Security, privacy and governance, plus availability, reliability and scalability of a managed service, can outweigh raw quality for regulated and customer-facing uses.
Customize in order of effort: prompting, then grounding, then tuning with labeled examples, and training from scratch only rarely; use cases sort into create, summarize, discover and automate.

quiz.q: A support team needs to sort a very high volume of messages into three simple categories quickly and at low cost. Which approach is best?
choices: Pick the largest available model, since it will always be the most accurate
Test a smaller, faster model tier on real samples and move up only if needed
Train a new model from scratch so that it learns only the three categories
Use a video generation model because it handles the highest message volume
quiz.explain: A simple, high-volume, latency-sensitive task favors a lighter tier, verified by testing. Choice A is tempting because bigger sounds safer, but larger models usually respond more slowly and cost more per request than this task needs.

quiz.q: A sales operations group wants employees to ask plain-language questions across scattered manuals and receive answers that link back to the source documents. Which use case type is this?
choices: Create, because the model writes new sentences for each answer it gives
Summarize, because the long manuals are reduced to a few key points
Automate, because the model carries out a repeated step in a workflow
Discover, because people find and verify information across large collections
quiz.explain: Question answering over scattered content with citations is the discover use case. Choice A is tempting because the answers are generated text, but the business purpose is finding and verifying information rather than producing new content.

days.recap: Pick a model by modality, context window, security and governance, availability and reliability, performance versus cost, and the customization effort you can afford (prompting, grounding, tuning); then map the need to the four use case verbs: create, summarize, discover and automate.

days.title: Data in Gen AI, the Five Layers, and Google's Foundation Models

concepts.heading: Data Types and Business Implications
concepts.body: Data comes in types, and each has business implications for gen AI. Structured data follows a predefined schema of rows and columns with set data types, so it is easy to store in tables and query with SQL. Unstructured data has no predefined data model: emails and documents, images, audio, video and scanned pages. It is hard to query with SQL and historically much of it went unused. Foundation models, especially multimodal ones, can read and generate unstructured content directly, which opens archives that traditional analytics could not use, such as call recordings or contract text. Both need governance: privacy rules, access control and checks that content is accurate. Labeled data pairs each example with the answer a model should learn, such as an email and its category, and is used in supervised learning and to tune a model. Unlabeled data has no such answers, supports unsupervised learning, and is what foundation models are pre-trained on in very large amounts.

concepts.heading: Data Quality and Accessibility
concepts.body: Data quality determines how useful and trustworthy gen AI output is, and poor data leads to poor output. The guide lists six characteristics. Completeness asks whether required values are present. Consistency means the same fact is recorded the same way everywhere: the same units, spellings and date formats. Relevance asks whether the data relates to the task; a policy assistant needs the current approved policy, while brochures and old drafts add noise and outdated rules. Availability, also called accessibility, asks whether authorized people and systems can reach the data when needed; silos are a common obstacle, because models and agents that cannot reach data cannot use it. Format affects how easily tools can read the data: scans and handwriting often need preparation such as text extraction. Cost is part of planning, because collecting, cleaning and labeling take time and money.

concepts.heading: The Five Layers of the Gen AI Landscape
concepts.body: Leaders compare offerings more easily when they sort them into five layers, each building on the one below. Infrastructure is the compute that trains and runs models: data centers, accelerators such as GPUs and Google's TPUs, networking and storage. Models are the foundation models that understand and generate content, for example Gemini for multimodal tasks. Platforms are where developers find, tune, ground, evaluate and deploy models; on Google Cloud this is Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI. Agents are systems built on models that pursue a goal, plan steps and use tools or data to act. Applications are finished products people use directly, such as Gemini for Google Workspace. The central trade-off is speed against control. Higher layers are closer to ready to use, with little to build and fast time to value, but fewer ways to change behavior. Lower layers offer more control and customization but need skills, time and operation.

concepts.heading: Google's Models: Gemini and Gemma
concepts.body: The exam expects you to match a need to the right model family. Gemini is Google's general-purpose multimodal family. It can take in several kinds of input such as text, images, audio and video, and generate content such as text and code. It is the usual first choice for understanding and reasoning across mixed content, and also for text tasks such as summarizing long documents. Gemini also powers Google's own products, such as Gemini for Google Workspace. Gemma is Google's family of lightweight generative AI open models. Google documents that they can run in your applications and on your own hardware, mobile devices or hosted services, and because they are open weight, teams can tune them with the AI framework of their choice. Gemma models are available through Model Garden on the platform, where developers can try and deploy them. Choose Gemma when control matters: where it runs, how it is customized and how it fits existing infrastructure, for example inference on a device to reduce latency and data sent to a cloud service. The price of that control is more work in packaging, tuning, operating and updating.

concepts.heading: Google's Models: Imagen and Veo
concepts.body: Generative media models are specialized by output type, and output type is part of model choice. Imagen is the family built to create and edit still images. Google's image documentation lists text-to-image creation from a prompt, editing or expanding an image using a mask area you define, and upscaling to increase resolution. Gemini can also generate images as part of its multimodal abilities, but Imagen is the family dedicated to image generation and editing. Veo is Google's video generation model family. Documented capabilities include text to video, image to video starting from a first frame or from first and last frames, generating video from reference images, and extending videos. A campaign that needs both stills and video may need two model families, and both can be reached through the platform.

examPoints: Structured data has rows and columns, unstructured data covers text, images, audio and video, labeled data carries the answer for supervised learning, and unlabeled data is what foundation models pre-train on.

Quality characteristics are completeness, consistency, relevance, availability, format and cost; the five layers are infrastructure, models, platforms, agents and applications, with higher layers faster and lower layers more controllable.
Gemini is the multimodal general-purpose family, Gemma is the open family you run and tune yourself, Imagen makes and edits images, and Veo makes video.

quiz.q: A company merges customer records from three systems and finds the same product written in several different ways and dates in mixed formats, so its assistant gives unreliable answers. Which data quality characteristic is the main problem?
choices: Consistency, because the same facts are recorded in different ways across systems
Completeness, because some records are missing required values entirely
Cost, because collecting data from several systems is expensive to maintain
Availability, because authorized staff cannot reach the merged records at all
quiz.explain: The same item and date written differently is a consistency problem, fixed by standards and cleaning. Choice B is tempting because messy data often has gaps too, but the scenario describes values that are present and written in conflicting ways, not missing values.

quiz.q: A marketing team wants to produce short draft video concepts from a text brief. Which Google model family is built for this?
choices: Gemma, because open models are the right choice for any creative content
Imagen, because it is Google's family for creating still images from prompts
Veo, because it is Google's video generation model family
Gemini, because only a general-purpose multimodal family can handle all media
quiz.explain: Veo is the family dedicated to video generation, including text to video. Choice B is tempting because Imagen is also a media generator, but it creates and edits still images, not motion over time.

days.recap: Data differs by type (structured, unstructured, labeled, unlabeled) and must be complete, consistent, relevant, available, readable and affordable; the gen AI landscape has five layers from infrastructure to applications, and Google's models are Gemini (multimodal), Gemma (open), Imagen (images) and Veo (video).

days.title: Google Cloud's Strengths in Gen AI

concepts.heading: AI-First Approach and an Integrated Ecosystem
concepts.body: The exam guide refers to Google's AI-first approach and asks how it turns into practical gen AI solutions. The business reading is that models, infrastructure and products come from one company, so advances reach customers inside offerings they can adopt. The related strength is integration across the ecosystem. Google's gen AI is not a single isolated tool. Gemini is built into products people already use, and Gemini Enterprise is described as an intranet search, AI assistant and agentic platform with prebuilt connectors to commonly used third-party applications such as Confluence, Jira, Microsoft SharePoint and ServiceNow. Google describes it as a single front door to AI for employees. Access is permissions-aware: people receive answers only from content they could already open.

concepts.heading: An Enterprise-Ready Platform
concepts.body: The exam guide lists five qualities of an enterprise-ready AI platform: responsible, secure, private, reliable and scalable. Privacy is usually the first question for regulated industries. In Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Google's terms state that Google will not use customer data to train or fine-tune any AI and ML models without the customer's prior permission or instruction, and this applies to the managed models on the platform. Privacy is not zero retention: some features, such as abuse-monitoring logs or Grounding with Google Search, can retain data for limited periods, so zero data retention needs specific steps. Security includes two levels of encryption control. Google encrypts customer content at rest by default and the customer does not manage those keys. Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), created and controlled in Cloud KMS, let the customer control protection level, location, rotation, usage and access. Reliable and scalable describe a managed service that handles serving, scaling and operations.

concepts.heading: The Open Approach
concepts.body: Google Cloud describes its approach to gen AI as open: the platform does not force one model on you. Model Garden on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is a library where teams discover, test, customize and deploy models and assets from Google and Google partners, including open-source models. Business benefits are choice, because you pick the best model for each task instead of the one model a vendor owns; less lock-in, because a model that falls behind can be replaced; and one place to work, because evaluation and deployment use one managed platform. The agent logic, tool connections and identity policies sit around the model, so they stay in place when the model changes, which keeps governance consistent and switching cost low. Openness also reaches standards. The agent platform natively supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and OpenAPI 3.0, so agents connect to existing databases and enterprise systems through widely used interfaces. If a question compares several model sources on one platform or worries about vendor lock-in, the answer is the open approach.

concepts.heading: AI-Optimized Infrastructure
concepts.body: The infrastructure strength is the compute underneath gen AI. Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) are Google's custom-developed application-specific integrated circuits built to accelerate machine learning. They suit models dominated by matrix computations, the core operation in neural networks, and have on-chip high-bandwidth memory. Google Cloud also offers NVIDIA GPUs, which fit models with many custom operations and medium-to-large models. AI Hypercomputer is Google Cloud's integrated supercomputing system for AI workloads and the unified portfolio for its AI infrastructure. It combines performance-optimized infrastructure (GPUs, TPUs, networking and storage), open software (optimized frameworks and orchestration such as Google Kubernetes Engine) and flexible consumption options for obtaining capacity. The design aims to maximize goodput, the measure of actual ML productivity, so accelerators spend more time on useful work, with reliability features such as automated hardware health monitoring. Infrastructure does not remove bias, replace evaluation or reduce the need for data.

concepts.heading: Control Over Data and Democratizing AI
concepts.body: Control over data covers security, privacy and governance, open and leading first-party models, and prebuilt and customizable solutions and agents. Google's customer data terms, CMEK, and least-privilege access are the building blocks. When many teams build agents, risks grow: duplicates, unknown agents and inconsistent security. Google Cloud describes central governance, where Agent Registry and Agent Gateway give IT visibility to index, manage and reuse agents and enforce policies through a single control plane, and each agent can have a cryptographically secure identity with least-privilege access. Democratizing AI means meeting users at their skill level so value does not wait for scarce specialists. Low-code and no-code tools with templates let business users create agents and automated processes; Agent Studio offers low-code templates. Pro-developer tools such as the Agent Development Kit (ADK) give engineers full control in code. Pre-trained models and APIs let a team add summarization or image generation to an app by calling a model, with customization such as prompt engineering, grounding or tuning only when needed. The benefit is shorter time to value and no in-house model-building team.

examPoints: Match the strength to the cue: model choice and lock-in point to the open approach; regulation and customer data point to the enterprise-ready platform; Gemini inside familiar tools points to the integrated ecosystem.
TPUs are Google's custom ML chips, GPUs are also offered, and AI Hypercomputer is the integrated AI infrastructure portfolio; infrastructure speeds training and serving but does not fix bias.
Control over data means no training on customer data without permission, CMEK, and governed agent identity; democratizing AI means low-code and no-code tools, pre-trained models and APIs.

quiz.q: A bank worries that today's best model may not be tomorrow's and wants to switch models without redoing security rules or agent connections. Which Google Cloud strength addresses this?
choices: The open approach, with many models in one catalog and policies kept around the model
AI-optimized infrastructure, since faster chips make every model interchangeable
Democratized AI, since low-code tools remove the need to ever choose a model
Integration across products, since Gemini is built into Google Workspace apps
quiz.explain: Choice of models from Google, partners and open source on one platform, with governance outside the model, is the open approach. Choice B is tempting because infrastructure is a real Google strength, but hardware speed does not address model switching or lock-in.

quiz.q: A regulated insurer asks what Google says about its customer prompts and data when it uses the managed models on the platform. What is the correct statement?
choices: Customer data is added to the shared models by default to improve them for every other user
Customer data is never stored by any feature, so zero retention happens automatically
Google does not use it to train or fine-tune models without prior permission or instruction
Google encrypts data only if the customer first manages every single key in Cloud KMS
quiz.explain: Google's terms say customer data is not used to train or fine-tune models without the customer's prior permission or instruction. Choice B is tempting because it sounds like the strongest privacy promise, but some features can retain data for limited periods, so zero retention needs specific steps.

days.recap: Google Cloud's gen AI strengths are an AI-first approach with an integrated ecosystem, an enterprise-ready platform (responsible, secure, private, reliable, scalable), an open approach with model choice, AI-optimized infrastructure (TPUs, GPUs, AI Hypercomputer), control over data and governance, and democratized AI through low-code tools, pre-trained models and APIs.

days.title: Prebuilt Offerings: Gemini Enterprise and Gemini for Google Workspace

concepts.heading: What Gemini Enterprise Is
concepts.body: Google Cloud describes Gemini Enterprise as an intranet search, AI assistant and agentic platform that empowers knowledge workers using data sources from across the organization. It is a prebuilt application: administrators deploy and manage the platform, configure security policies, assign user licenses and connect enterprise data sources, while app users search enterprise data and work with AI assistants and agents in the web and mobile apps. Three pieces are worth remembering. Search gives permissions-aware access to enterprise information from connected sources through a single multimodal search interface. The assistant answers questions, summarizes uploaded content and generates content. Agents are prebuilt and custom agents that carry out multi-step work. Because it is a product rather than a platform for developers, it sits in the applications layer of the landscape.

concepts.heading: Connectors, Search Across Company Data, and Grounded Answers
concepts.body: Gemini Enterprise adds three things. Connected company data comes through prebuilt connectors to applications such as Confluence, Jira, Microsoft SharePoint and ServiceNow. Built-in trust comes from single sign-on and user-level access, so answers respect who may see what. Central administration lets IT deploy the product and manage users. The assistant is the in-app chat box, grounded in the organization's data stores and following defined security, privacy and compliance safeguards. According to Google, it can answer queries and follow-up questions, ground answers in enterprise data with citations and optionally in public website data, analyze and summarize uploaded content such as PDFs and images, generate images from text prompts, and create reports with streamed research. Citations let the reader open the source and verify a claim.

concepts.heading: Agents, the Agent Gallery, Skills, and Actions
concepts.body: Search answers where information is and what it says. Actions go further: they let Gemini Enterprise perform direct tasks inside connected data sources. Google's example is an app connected to Google Calendar and Jira Cloud, where the assistant can create calendar events or edit Jira issues. Agents come from several sources. Google provides prebuilt agents, such as Core Assistant and Deep Research, found in the Agent Gallery. Business employees can create their own with Workflow Builder, an interactive no-code, low-code tool for single-step and multi-step agents, if an administrator enables it. Developers can build custom agents in code, for example with the Agent Development Kit, and an administrator registers them, including agents hosted on Agent Runtime or built with the Agent2Agent protocol. IT gets one place to oversee agents from Google, third parties and internal teams, and each agent has a state such as enabled, private, suspended or disabled. Skills are reusable instructions and standardized prompts, written in natural language, that customize how the assistant completes tasks such as reviewing contracts or writing in your brand voice. The assistant applies a skill automatically when it is relevant.

concepts.heading: Analytics and Notebooks
concepts.body: Gemini Enterprise is a product that IT runs, so IT needs evidence that people use it and that it works. Analytics gives insight into usage trends, search quality and end-user engagement of an app, in an interactive dashboard experience powered by Looker. Do not confuse it with observability, which is technical telemetry such as request traces and audit logs for diagnosing latency and monitoring agent steps. Skills, actions and agents are capabilities that employees use to do work; they do not report on usage. The exam guide also mentions notebook capabilities. Google describes the notebook offering as an AI-powered research and knowledge assistant that helps you summarize information, brainstorm ideas and write with confidence using notebooks that contain your notes, sources and ideas, and it can be used alongside the Gemini Enterprise experience.

concepts.heading: Gemini for Google Workspace, and the Gemini App
concepts.body: Gemini for Google Workspace is built into Gmail, Docs, Slides and Sheets, so people get Gemini assistance directly in the productivity apps they already use. Nothing has to be built and users stay in familiar apps. It is an in-app assistant for the document in front of the person. Gemini Enterprise is different: it hosts agents and searches across systems for the whole organization. Developers who need a differentiated application use the platform instead. The exam guide also lists the Gemini app and Gems under this objective; check the current guide for them. A useful decision test asks who the user is (an individual, an employee or a developer), where the work happens (a chat window, an office app, company systems or a custom product) and who manages it (the user, IT or a development team).

examPoints: Gemini Enterprise is an intranet search, AI assistant and agentic platform that IT deploys: connectors to company systems, permissions-aware search, prebuilt and custom agents, the Agent Gallery, skills, actions and analytics.
Employees without developer skills build agents with Workflow Builder, developers register custom agents, and analytics (not observability or skills) reports usage and search quality.
Gemini for Google Workspace is the in-app assistant for Gmail, Docs, Slides and Sheets; choose it for help inside documents and Gemini Enterprise for company-wide search and agents.

quiz.q: A company wants employees to search Confluence, Jira and SharePoint from one place, with answers limited to what each person may already access. Which offering fits?
choices: Gemini for Google Workspace, because it adds writing help inside Docs and Gmail
Gemini Enterprise, because it connects company data and respects user permissions
A diffusion image model, because every answer must be generated as a picture
Training a new foundation model, because search needs the company's own model
quiz.explain: Gemini Enterprise connects to company systems through prebuilt connectors and gives permissions-aware search and agents. Choice A is tempting because both products use Gemini, but the Workspace assistant helps inside its own apps rather than searching other company systems.

quiz.q: A finance manager wants to automate a repeated approval process herself, without writing code, and let colleagues use it. Which Gemini Enterprise capability suits this?
choices: Analytics, which shows dashboards of usage and search quality for IT
Observability, which provides request traces and audit logs for developers
Agent Development Kit, which is a code framework for professional engineers
Workflow Builder, which lets employees create no-code or low-code agents
quiz.explain: Workflow Builder is the no-code, low-code tool for business employees to create and manage agents. Choice C is tempting because the Agent Development Kit also builds agents, but it is used in code by developers, not by a manager without programming skills.

days.recap: Gemini Enterprise is the prebuilt company-wide search, assistant and agent platform (connectors, Agent Gallery, Workflow Builder, skills, actions, analytics and notebooks), Gemini for Google Workspace is the in-app assistant in Gmail, Docs, Slides and Sheets, and the guide also lists the Gemini app and Gems.

days.title: Customer Experience: Search and the Customer Engagement Suite

concepts.heading: Finding Information Versus Completing a Task
concepts.body: Customer-experience needs fall into a few families, each with its own offering. Search is for a customer who asks a question and gets relevant results or a generated answer drawn from content; the goal is to find or understand information. Agent Search covers this. Conversational Agents, part of the Customer Engagement Suite, are virtual agents that hold a dialogue, collect the details they need, call other systems and escalate to a person; the goal is to get something done, such as booking, changing or looking up a record. Agent Assist supports a human representative who is already on a contact. Conversational Insights analyzes conversations that already happened. Ask what the customer must actually do: only find and understand approved information points to Agent Search, completing tasks through dialogue points to Conversational Agents, and running the whole contact center points to Contact Center as a Service. Choose the smallest offering that meets the need.

concepts.heading: External Search: Agent Search and Google Search Grounding
concepts.body: Agent Search, formerly Vertex AI Search, lets organizations, including those with limited machine learning skills, build Google-quality search experiences over their own content. It provides semantic search; recommendations that find content similar to what a visitor is viewing; and generative answers and summaries with conversational search. Teams can embed the result in a website through a widget. The data source matters because answers should come from material the business approves. Grounding connects a model to an outside source at answer time, since a model knows only what was in its training data and can be out of date. Grounding with Google Search connects the model to world knowledge across a wide range of topics or to up-to-date information on the internet, and the data is publicly available web data. It suits open-ended, current questions where the company holds no private source, and is wrong for questions whose answer is the company's own rule. Agent Search over content the organization chooses gives accuracy and control, at the cost of the open web's breadth.

concepts.heading: Customer Engagement Suite: Conversational Agents and Agent Assist
concepts.body: The Customer Engagement Suite groups Google Cloud products that apply AI to customer service. Current documentation presents the suite under the name Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience and the agent builder as CX Agent Studio; this plan uses the exam guide's names. Conversational Agents provide proactive, personalized self-service through virtual agents that take on routine inquiries and escalate to a person, so representatives can focus on specialized calls. Agent Assist is the offering for that. While a representative is on a call or chat, it can transcribe the conversation in real time, recommend ready-to-send responses and next steps, surface answers from a centralized knowledge base, translate live and produce a summary at the end. A virtual agent replaces or defers a human contact; Agent Assist supports one who is already on the contact.

concepts.heading: Conversational Insights and Contact Center as a Service
concepts.body: Contact centers produce unstructured data: call recordings and chat transcripts. Conversational Insights, called Customer Experience Insights in current documentation, lets a business import that data and run analytics on it. It can identify call topics, entities and caller and representative sentiment, flag interesting interactions for review. It can import conversations from Conversational Agents and Agent Assist, which closes the loop between serving customers and improving service. Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) is for a business that needs the whole contact center rather than one capability. It is a turnkey, cloud-native, omnichannel solution covering voice, chat, SMS, email and in-app experiences, AI-driven routing, an agent desktop that can work inside a CRM, and workforce and quality management such as scheduling, forecasting and coaching. It uses the suite's building blocks.

concepts.heading: Mapping the Customer Journey and Picking the Offering
concepts.body: A useful way to remember the suite is along the timeline of a contact. Before or instead of a human, Conversational Agents provide self-service. During a human contact, Agent Assist coaches the representative with suggested responses, knowledge-base answers, summaries and translation. After contacts, Conversational Insights analyzes conversation data for topics, sentiment and areas to improve. Contact Center as a Service brings these together in a single platform. Agent Search sits beside this timeline as the offering for content-based search and answers on a website or app, and Grounding with Google Search is a way for a model to reach public web information, not a customer service product on its own. Answering questions from the company's own documents on a customer-facing site is Agent Search. A voice agent that checks an order and arranges a return is a Conversational Agents use case, a dialogue plus actions in backend systems. Helping a live representative in a language they do not speak is Agent Assist. Finding calls with angry customers across thousands of recordings is Conversational Insights. Running voice, chat and email together with routing and workforce tools is Contact Center as a Service.

examPoints: Agent Search finds and answers from content you choose (semantic search, recommendations, generative answers, widget); Grounding with Google Search uses public web data for current, world-knowledge questions.

Conversational Agents complete tasks through dialogue, Agent Assist helps a live representative, Conversational Insights analyzes finished conversations, and Contact Center as a Service is the whole omnichannel platform.
Choose the smallest offering that meets the need: finding information is search, getting something done is a virtual agent, and company-specific facts need approved content rather than the open web.

quiz.q: A hospital group wants a public-website assistant that answers questions only from its own approved health pages, without booking or changing records. What is the simplest fit?
choices: Contact Center as a Service, because it supports voice, chat and email channels together
Agent Search over the approved content, with generative answers and a website widget
Grounding with Google Search, because public web data gives the widest possible coverage
Conversational Insights, because it analyzes topics across many recorded conversations
quiz.explain: The need is finding and understanding information from approved content, which Agent Search does with semantic search, generative answers and a widget. Choice C is tempting because wider coverage sounds helpful, but grounding on the open web risks answers from outside sources instead of approved pages.

quiz.q: A call center manager wants a live translation feature and suggested replies for representatives who are already speaking with customers. Which offering is designed for this moment?
choices: Conversational Insights, which reviews topics and sentiment after calls have ended
Conversational Agents, which handle routine contacts without any representative
Agent Search, which builds search and recommendations on a company website
Agent Assist, which supports a representative during a live call or chat
quiz.explain: Agent Assist works during the live contact with real-time suggestions, knowledge answers, summaries and translation. Choice B is tempting because it is also in the suite, but Conversational Agents replace or defer a human contact instead of supporting a representative who is on one.

days.recap: For customers, Agent Search answers from approved content and Grounding with Google Search from the public web; the Customer Engagement Suite adds Conversational Agents for self-service, Agent Assist for live representatives, Conversational Insights for analysis and Contact Center as a Service for the whole omnichannel contact center.

days.title: Building with AI: Agent Platform, RAG, and Custom Agents

concepts.heading: Agent Platform and Model Garden
concepts.body: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, the current name of what was Vertex AI, is Google Cloud's platform for building with AI. Google describes it as an open, comprehensive platform to build, scale, govern and optimize enterprise agents grounded in enterprise data. Build means ADK or other frameworks, Agent Studio for low-code design, Model Garden for models, RAG Engine and Vector Search. Scale means Agent Runtime, the managed place to deploy and scale agents. Govern means access control through IAM, content security and policies for safe behavior. Model Garden is the model catalog and a single place to discover, test and deploy. It offers Google models such as Gemini and Gemma, partner models from other AI companies and open-weights models. Partner and open models can be consumed as managed APIs, called Model as a Service, where Google runs the infrastructure and developers just call the API, or open models can be deployed to an endpoint when the team needs more control over serving. If the question is which model to use, think Model Garden; training a new classifier on your own labels is a different job.

concepts.heading: Agent Platform AutoML
concepts.body: AutoML on Agent Platform trains models for common prediction tasks, such as classifying images or predicting values from tabular data, without the user writing training code. The user supplies a labeled dataset and picks an objective, and the platform tries approaches and tunes the model automatically. In Google's comparison of training methods, AutoML needs no data-science expertise and no programming ability, and takes less time than custom training because little data preparation and no development are needed. The trade-off is control. AutoML requires you to target one of its predefined objectives, you cannot manually tune hyperparameters, and control of the training environment is limited to things such as a training-hour budget. Custom training means you write the training application, so you can target any objective, use any algorithm, define your own loss functions or metrics, and choose machine types and containers. AutoML is for predictive models from labeled data, not for retrieving text for a language model or hosting agents.

concepts.heading: Agent Search and Prebuilt RAG
concepts.body: A large language model does not know an organization's private knowledge such as policies, manuals and contracts. Without it the model may guess, which produces hallucinations. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) fixes this without retraining: at question time the system retrieves relevant passages from the organization's data and adds them to the prompt as context. Google Cloud offers two ways to get RAG. Prebuilt RAG with Agent Search is a managed search-and-answer product. Agent Search lets developers build Google-quality search and recommendation experiences over their own content, including public websites and private data stores, even with limited ML skills. You connect your content and get ingestion, indexing, semantic retrieval and generated answers out of the box, plus a console, API and embeddable widget. It has variants for custom search, media search and recommendations, and healthcare search for FHIR health records. Choose it when you want a finished experience over your content quickly.

concepts.heading: RAG APIs: RAG Engine
concepts.body: The second offering is the RAG APIs on Agent Platform, delivered as RAG Engine, a data framework for building context-augmented LLM applications. It is aimed at developers who build their own application and want control of data transformation, the corpora and how retrieved context is passed to the model or agent, instead of wiring every step themselves. RAG Engine describes the process as a sequence. Data ingestion brings data in from sources such as local files, Cloud Storage and Google Drive. Data transformation converts it for indexing, for example by splitting it into chunks. Embedding turns text into numbers that capture meaning, so related text lies close together. Indexing builds an index, called a corpus, optimized for searching. Retrieval finds the passages that match the question. Generation gives those passages to the model as context so it writes a grounded answer. Refreshing the index is far cheaper than retraining a model. The decision rule is speed and low effort for prebuilt Agent Search, and custom control and integration into application logic for the developer-oriented RAG APIs.

concepts.heading: Building Custom Agents: ADK, Agent Studio, and Agent Runtime
concepts.body: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform supports teams that build their own agents. The Agent Development Kit (ADK) is an open-source, modular, model-agnostic framework that makes building and deploying agents feel like standard software development, scaling from simple tasks to complex, multi-step and multi-agent workflows. Developers may also use any other open-source framework and any model accessible through Model Garden, Gemini or otherwise. Agent Studio is the low-code option: a visual canvas for designing, prototyping and managing agent workflows without writing code. Agent Runtime, formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine, is a managed runtime to deploy, manage and scale agents with built-in observability and no servers for the team to manage; agents can be deployed from source files or container images. Use a simple match: Model Garden picks the model, ADK builds in code, Agent Studio designs low-code, RAG or Agent Search supplies company knowledge, and Agent Runtime hosts and scales the agent.

examPoints: Model Garden answers which model to use (Google, partner and open models, managed API or endpoint); AutoML trains predictive models from labeled data without code; custom training is needed for nonstandard objectives.

Prebuilt RAG with Agent Search is the fast, managed path with a widget; the RAG APIs (RAG Engine) give developers control over ingestion, chunking, corpora and retrieval; RAG changes the prompt context, not the model.
For custom agents, ADK builds in code, Agent Studio designs low-code, and Agent Runtime deploys and scales the finished agent with built-in observability.

quiz.q: A marketing team with no programmers has a labeled table of past customers and wants a model that predicts which customers will leave. Which Agent Platform capability fits best?
choices: Agent Runtime, because it hosts and scales agents for production use
Model Garden, because it is where a team discovers models from Google and partners
AutoML, because it trains a model from labeled data without writing code
RAG Engine, because it retrieves passages from company documents for answers
quiz.explain: AutoML trains predictive models from a labeled dataset without code or deep data-science skill. Choice B is tempting because Model Garden also has models, but it is a catalog for discovering and deploying existing models, not for training a classifier on your own labels.

quiz.q: A developer team wants to control chunking, corpora and how retrieved text reaches the model inside its own application. A different team wants a finished website answer experience quickly. Which pairing is right?
choices: RAG Engine for the first team and prebuilt RAG with Agent Search for the second
Agent Search for the first team and RAG Engine for the second team
Agent Runtime for the first team and Model Garden for the second team
Agent Studio for the first team and AutoML for the second team
quiz.explain: RAG Engine is the developer-oriented framework with control of the pipeline, while Agent Search is the prebuilt managed product with a widget. Choice B is tempting because it reverses the pairing, but a team needing fine control would be limited by a finished product and a team wanting speed would face needless work.

days.recap: On Agent Platform, Model Garden is the model catalog, AutoML trains predictive models without code, RAG comes prebuilt with Agent Search or as developer RAG APIs (RAG Engine), and custom agents are built with ADK or low-code Agent Studio and run on managed Agent Runtime.

days.title: Agent Tooling: Tool Types, Pre-Built AI APIs, and Where to Build

concepts.heading: Why an Agent Needs Tools
concepts.body: A language model reads text and writes text. It does not know today's order status, and it cannot book a pickup or issue a refund by itself. An agent wraps the model in a loop: it reasons about a goal, decides on a step, uses a tool to carry out that step, reads the result and continues until the goal is met. Tools are the agent's bridge to the outside world, and Google's function-calling documentation describes two main jobs for them. The first is fetching data, such as an order record or a knowledge-base article, so the answer is current instead of guessed. The second is taking action, such as submitting a form, updating a record or handing a conversation to a person. A model alone can only talk, while an agent with tools can look things up and get work done in company systems. Treat extensions and plugins generically, as add-on connections that give an agent a capability.

concepts.heading: Tool Types: API Tools, Function Tools, and Data Stores
concepts.body: Three common tool types in Google Cloud's agent products: An API tool gives the agent a description of an API, for example an OpenAPI tool in Conversational Agents, and by default the agent calls that API on your behalf. A function tool works through function calling: the model is told which functions exist, and when it needs one it outputs structured data with the function name and parameters. Your own application then runs the function and hands the result back to the model, so the model proposes and your code executes. A data store is different because it is about reading knowledge, not running operations. The agent retrieves passages from indexed company content such as PDFs, web pages or tables, which is the retrieval pattern applied to an agent. Rule of thumb: questions about documents point to a data store, while looking up or changing a record in a live system points to an API or function tool. If a security team wants its own code to stay in control of a call for authorization or auditing, function calling keeps execution on the client side.

concepts.heading: Storage, Databases, and Code as Tool Back Ends
concepts.body: Agents are only as useful as the places they can reach. Cloud Storage holds unstructured files such as PDFs and images, and BigQuery or other databases hold structured records. An Agent Search data store can be built from Cloud Storage, BigQuery or website content, so those services are the usual homes of an agent's knowledge. Storage only holds data; it decides nothing. When an agent needs a company-specific rule, such as whether a repair is covered under a warranty given a serial number and purchase date, a team writes a small piece of code and exposes it as a callable endpoint. Cloud Run functions, the current name for what was called Cloud Functions, runs single-purpose code without servers to manage. Cloud Run fits when the logic is a larger containerized service. To the agent, either one looks like an API or function tool that takes inputs and returns an answer.

concepts.heading: Pre-Built AI APIs as Ready-Made Tools
concepts.body: Google Cloud also offers pre-trained APIs that an agent can call without anyone training a model. Speech-to-Text turns audio into text and Text-to-Speech turns text into audio, which together give a voice agent ears and a mouth. Cloud Translation handles text, and its Advanced edition adds glossaries and Document Translation, which keeps the layout of formatted files such as PDF and DOCX. Document AI turns unstructured documents such as invoices and receipts into structured fields for a database. The Cloud Vision API analyzes images: labels, logos, text and explicit content. The Natural Language API analyzes text for sentiment, entities, entity sentiment and categories. Benefits are speed to value, no data scientists needed and managed scale; limits are that a generic API may not know specialized vocabulary and governance still applies to what you send. Lifecycle warning: the Video Intelligence API is deprecated (shutdown September 2027), and Google recommends moving to a multimodal Gemini model, which can reason over video, images, audio and text in one request.

concepts.heading: Agent Studio versus Google AI Studio
concepts.body: The guide asks when to use each of two similar-sounding tools. Google AI Studio is a web-based tool where developers, students and researchers prototype prompts in a browser and get started with the Gemini Developer API; it is the quick path for personal experiments. Agent Studio belongs to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, the managed Google Cloud platform for building, scaling, governing and optimizing enterprise agents. In Agent Studio you design agents and interact with models without code, inside a Google Cloud project where the company's own security and governance controls apply. Code-first teams use the Agent Development Kit on the same platform. Think of the contrast as prototype versus governed enterprise agents: a solo developer trying an idea in an afternoon points to Google AI Studio; business analysts designing an agent in the company's controlled cloud project point to Agent Studio.

examPoints: A question about an agent that must look up or change a record in a live system is testing API or function tools, while a question about answering from documents is testing data stores and retrieval.

A question that names an input type and an output type, such as audio to text, invoices to fields, or photos to labels, is testing which pre-built API matches: Speech-to-Text, Document AI or Cloud Vision API. For video archives, remember that the Video Intelligence API is deprecated and a multimodal Gemini model is the path.
A question that contrasts quick personal prototyping with governed enterprise agents is testing Google AI Studio versus Agent Studio on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

quiz.q: A bank wants an agent to look up a customer's balance, but its security team requires that its own application code execute every call to the core banking system. Which tool approach fits?
choices: A data store built from the bank's policy documents, so the agent retrieves balance answers from indexed pages
Function calling, where the model names the function and parameters and the application runs the call
An API tool configured so the agent calls the banking API on its own with the stored schema
Speech-to-Text, so the agent can transcribe the customer's spoken request before it answers
quiz.explain: With function calling the model only proposes a call as structured data and the application executes it, which keeps authorization and auditing in the bank's code. Choice C is tempting because API tools also reach live systems, but by default the agent makes that call itself.

quiz.q: A retailer wants an agent to read supplier invoices that arrive as scans and PDFs in many layouts and pass structured records to its finance system. Which pre-built API fits best?
choices: Document AI, which turns unstructured documents into structured fields such as totals and dates
Natural Language API, which finds sentiment and entities in free text written by customers
Text-to-Speech, which turns the invoice text into audio that a clerk can listen to
Cloud Run functions, which stores the scanned files until a person types in the fields
quiz.explain: Document AI is built to transform documents such as invoices into structured data using processors that digitize, extract and classify. Choice B is tempting because it also analyzes text, but it returns sentiment and entities, not named invoice fields.

days.recap: Agents use tools to fetch data and take action: API tools, function tools and data stores. Cloud Storage and databases hold data, Cloud Run functions and Cloud Run hold custom logic, and pre-built APIs cover speech, translation, documents, images and text. Video Intelligence is deprecated, so use a multimodal Gemini model. Google AI Studio is for prototyping; Agent Studio is for governed enterprise agents.

days.title: Foundation Model Limitations, Remedies, and Continuous Monitoring

concepts.heading: Common Limitations of Foundation Models
concepts.body: The guide names six limitations. Data dependency means a model can only reflect the data it learned from, so languages, dialects or topics that are thin in the training data get weaker results. The knowledge cutoff is the point in time where training stopped. Anything later, such as a regulation that took effect last month, is unknown to the model even though it answers fluently. Bias means the model can pick up and even amplify stereotypes and unequal treatment found in its data. Fairness is the matching goal: avoiding unjust impact on people, especially across sensitive characteristics. A hallucination is fluent, confident content that is invented, such as fake citations, wrong numbers or products that do not exist. Edge cases are rare or unusual inputs, such as mixed languages, odd formats or boundary questions, where a model that passes typical tests can still fail.

concepts.heading: Google-Recommended Remedies
concepts.body: Different limitations call for different remedies, and the exam rewards matching them. Grounding and retrieval-augmented generation connect the model to current, trusted sources, so they fix stale facts and reduce hallucination while adding links to sources. Prompt engineering is the cheapest first step: clear instructions, supplied context and permission to say that it does not know discourage guessing. Fine-tuning teaches specialized language, tone or domain depth when instructions are not enough, but it bakes in knowledge at one point in time, so it is a poor fix for facts that change hourly. Human in the loop, usually shortened to HITL, places a person's judgment between model output and consequence, and it is recommended wherever errors have regulatory, financial or personal impact. No single setting removes hallucinations and a newer or bigger model is never a guarantee. Bias is handled by measuring outputs for equivalent inputs across groups, and improving and balancing data. Removing one field rarely removes bias because other inputs can act as proxies.

concepts.heading: Evaluating and Versioning Models
concepts.body: Google recommends continuous monitoring and evaluation, and it starts with evaluation before any change. Newer models are not better on every task and can change tone, length and format. The Gen AI evaluation service on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform gives objective, data-driven assessment and supports tasks such as model migrations, prompt editing and fine-tuning. Keep a representative evaluation set with typical, difficult and edge-case inputs, agree on metrics, then compare old and new on the same data before changing production. Model Registry keeps multiple versions of a model under one name, lets you assign a default version and compare versions, so a team can point back to an earlier one when a new version underperforms. The same discipline applies to prompts and configurations. Informal impressions are weak evidence for an upgrade, while never upgrading means missing improvements and eventually reaching a retirement date.

concepts.heading: Model Lifecycle, Patches, and Updates
concepts.body: Foundation models on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform have a lifecycle. Google publishes release dates and retirement dates with recommended replacement models, and when a model is scheduled for retirement it posts a fixed date in advance. Pinning to a specific model version gives stable behavior until it retires, but it does not keep the model alive forever. The sensible routine is to track the lifecycle page, move to the recommended replacement and test mission-critical features with the evaluation set before deploying. Patching follows who operates the software, as in Google Cloud's shared responsibility model. With a managed model API, Google operates and updates the serving infrastructure, while the customer manages its own application, access controls, data and prompts and tracks announced retirements. With a self-operated deployment, such as an open model in your own containers, the customer maintains images, libraries and serving software and applies security patches on a schedule.

concepts.heading: Drift, Skew, KPIs, and Feature Store
concepts.body: A model that is up and fast can still be wrong, so monitoring must look at data and results, not only uptime. Drift happens when real-world data changes over time, such as new customer habits or seasonality, and accuracy quietly falls. Model Monitoring (the generally available v1 offering, for models deployed to an endpoint) watches for two related effects. Training-serving skew means production feature data differs from the data used for training. Inference drift means production feature data changes significantly over time. You set alert thresholds against a baseline; crossing them tells you to re-evaluate or retrain. Key performance indicators make performance tracking concrete: business outcomes such as resolution rate and customer satisfaction, quality scores on a regular evaluation set, rate of unsafe answers, and operational health such as latency, errors and cost per interaction. Feature Store on the platform is a managed service for feature management and online serving; drawing training and serving features from one managed place helps avoid skew.

examPoints: A question describing confident but invented citations is testing hallucination, while one describing outdated answers about recent events is testing the knowledge cutoff; the matching remedies are verification plus grounding in both cases.
A question about facts that change often versus a brand voice or specialist depth is testing grounding or RAG for changing facts, and prompts or fine-tuning for style and domain behavior.
A question about accuracy falling months after launch while the service stays healthy is testing drift and skew monitoring with alert thresholds, plus KPIs, versioning and evaluation before upgrades.

quiz.q: A company's claims assistant describes insurance rules that were replaced last month, and it sounds completely sure of itself. What is the most likely limitation and the recommended remedy?
choices: Bias in the training data, so the company should remove sensitive fields from every prompt
A knowledge cutoff, so the assistant should be grounded in current, trusted company sources
Edge cases in the inputs, so the company should lower the limit on output length
Data leakage from tuning, so the company should delete the model and train a new one
quiz.explain: The model's training stopped at a point in time, so rules that changed afterward are unknown to it; grounding or RAG supplies current sources at request time. Choice A is tempting because bias is a named limitation, but nothing in the scenario describes unfair treatment of any group.

quiz.q: A retail demand-forecasting model was accurate at launch. Eight months later forecasts are consistently off, although the service shows no errors and responds quickly. What should the team set up?
choices: A larger quota for prediction requests, so the service can serve many more users at the same time
A change to the endpoint so that an older model version is the one shown to users instead
